headline: Seaside emails, a kind runner and the tablet test
teaser: Where did Sofia go on holiday? Why did Jonas stop in the middle of a race? Which is better for homework, a tablet or a laptop?

articles.title: Emails from the Seaside
articles.dek: Mateo asks lots of questions about his cousin's summer holiday.
paras: Hi Sofia, How was your holiday in Portugal? Did you have good weather? Did you swim in the sea? I didn't go anywhere in the summer. I stayed at home and played games. Please tell me everything! Love, Mateo

Hi Mateo, Thanks for your email. We had a great time! The weather was hot and sunny, so we went to the beach every day. I didn't swim much on the first day because the water was very cold. On the second day, I jumped in and I loved it! Love, Sofia
Hi Sofia, Wow, that sounds great! Did you eat any local food? What did you do in the evenings? Did you take many photos? Please send me some. Love, Mateo

Hi Mateo, Yes, I ate fish and fresh bread every day. I didn't like the soup, but Dad loved it. In the evenings, we walked along the harbour and watched the boats. I took more than a hundred photos! My brother didn't take any because he lost his phone on the bus. Love, Sofia
Hi Sofia, Poor Leo! Did he find his phone in the end? Where did you stay? Did you sleep in a hotel? Love, Mateo

Hi Mateo, He didn't find it, but the bus driver found it and called us the next day. We didn't stay in a hotel. We stayed in a small flat near the beach, and it was cheap and nice. Next summer, come with us! Love, Sofia

articles.title: The Last Lap
articles.dek: Jonas is running the race of his life, and then someone falls.
paras: Last Saturday was the school sports day. Jonas was standing at the start line when the teacher blew her whistle. He was nervous, but he wanted to win the 800 metres race for his class. It was a sunny day, and the whole school was watching from the field.

At first, everything went well. While the other runners were racing at the front, Jonas ran slowly behind them. His coach was shouting, "Wait! Keep your energy for the end!" Jonas liked this plan, but it was hard to run so slowly.

On the last lap, Jonas started to run faster. He was passing the third runner when something happened. A girl called Priya was running next to him. Her shoe came off, and she fell on the track. She cried out in pain.

Jonas stopped. The crowd was cheering loudly when he turned back. He gave Priya his hand and helped her stand up. "Are you OK?" he asked. Her knee was hurting, but she smiled. "Thank you," she said quietly.

While they were walking to the finish line, the other runners were crossing it. Everybody was clapping. Jonas and Priya finished last, but nobody was laughing. Priya's friends ran to her and gave her some water.
Later, the teacher was holding a big gold cup when she walked onto the field. "This prize is for the best sportsman of the day," she said. Then she gave it to Jonas.
Jonas was smiling when his friends ran to hug him. He didn't win the race, but he felt like a winner.

articles.title: Tablet or Laptop?
articles.dek: One class tried both for two weeks. Which one is better for homework?
paras: Many students use a laptop or a tablet for homework. Some students buy a new one every year. But which one is better? Our class tried both for two weeks. We wrote down what we liked and what we did not like. This is what we found.
A tablet is lighter than a laptop, so it is easier to carry to school. It is also cheaper. A good tablet costs about 200 euros, but a good laptop costs about 500.
However, a laptop has a bigger screen and a real keyboard. Typing is faster, and long homework is more comfortable. Most of us said that the laptop was more useful for writing.

Tablets are better for reading and drawing. You can read on the sofa or in bed, and you can draw with your finger. It is also nice to show a picture to a friend. The battery of a tablet also lasts longer than the battery of a laptop.
What about the price? A laptop is more expensive, so students must be more careful with it. Many of us were afraid to drop it. Nobody was afraid of dropping a tablet in a soft case.
Our teacher says that no machine is perfect. "The best choice depends on you," she says. If you write a lot, a laptop is a better friend. If you read and draw, a tablet is better.

The vote was not close, but nobody said that one machine is always the winner. So, which one do we like more? In our class, ten students chose the laptop and fourteen chose the tablet. What is your choice?
